items.followUp: What medicinal substance is obtained from the bark of the Cinchona tree, and what disease does it treat?

rubric.why: Identifies the important medicinal product or its use.
rubric.description: Names quinine, or states its use against malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either key fact.

rubric.why: Connects the medicinal product to its source.
rubric.description: Identifies Cinchona bark as the source.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the bark or the Cinchona tree.

modelAnswer: Quinine is used to treat malaria.

items.followUp: State two observations that helped A.F.A. King suggest a connection between mosquitoes and malaria.

rubric.why: Recognises the observed association between mosquitoes and malaria.
rubric.description: States that malaria was common where mosquitoes were abundant or present.

rubric.why: Gives another observation relating mosquito exposure to malaria.
rubric.description: States that protection from mosquito bites was associated with fewer malaria cases, or that mosquito bites were linked to malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant second observation.

modelAnswer: Malaria was common in places where mosquitoes were abundant.
People protected from mosquito bites, for example by mosquito nets, were less likely to get malaria.

items.followUp: Define magnification and resolving power in relation to a microscope.

rubric.why: Defines magnification as enlargement of the image.
rubric.description: States that magnification tells how much larger the image is than the object.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Defines resolving power in terms of distinguishing detail.
rubric.description: States that resolving power is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

modelAnswer: Magnification is how many times larger an image is than the object.
Resolving power is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate points.

items.followUp: Write the three main statements of the cell theory.

rubric.why: States that cells make up organisms.
rubric.description: All organisms are composed of one or more cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that organisms are made of cells.

rubric.why: States the central role of the cell in living things.
rubric.description: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.

modelAnswer: All organisms are composed of one or more cells.
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.

items.followUp: What is a taxon? Give two examples of taxa.

rubric.why: Shows that a taxon is a classification group or category.
rubric.description: Defines a taxon as a group or category used in biological classification.

rubric.why: Provides two valid examples of taxa.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct examples.

modelAnswer: A taxon is a group or category used in biological classification.
Two taxa are species and genus.

items.followUp: What is binomial nomenclature? Name the scientist who introduced it.

rubric.why: Identifies the two-part scientific naming system.
rubric.description: Defines binomial nomenclature as naming each organism with a two-word scientific name.

rubric.why: Identifies the scientist who introduced the system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct name.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature is the system of giving each organism a two-word scientific name: its genus name and species name.
It was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus.

items.followUp: Explain the difference between karyokinesis and cytokinesis.

rubric.why: Identifies the part of the cell that divides during karyokinesis.
rubric.description: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Identifies the part of the cell that divides during cytokinesis.
rubric.description: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

modelAnswer: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.

items.followUp: What source of energy does chlorophyll absorb for photosynthesis?

rubric.why: States chlorophyll's role in capturing light.
rubric.description: Chlorophyll absorbs or traps light energy from the Sun.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it captures light energy.

rubric.why: Explains the use or conversion of the captured energy.
rubric.description: The captured energy is used in photosynthesis and converted into chemical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the captured light energy to photosynthesis or chemical energy.

modelAnswer: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy from the Sun.
This energy is used in photosynthesis and converted into chemical energy.
